tasks.title: Native American Agriculture in the Arid Southwest
paras: In past centuries, Native Americans living in the arid areas of what is now the southwestern United States relied on a variety of strategies to ensure the success of their agriculture. First and foremost, water was the critical factor. The soil was rich because there was little rain to leach out the minerals, but the low precipitation caused its own problems. Long periods of drought could have made agriculture impossible; on the other hand, a sudden flood could just as easily have destroyed a crop.

Several techniques were developed to solve the water problem. The simplest was to plant crops in the floodplains and wait for the annual floods to water the young crops. A less dangerous technique was to build dikes or dams to control the flooding. These dikes both protected the plants against excessive flooding and prevented the water from escaping too quickly once it had arrived. The Hopi people designed their fields in a checkerboard pattern, with many small dikes, each enclosing only one or two stalks of maize (corn), while other groups built a series of dams to control the floods.

Another strategy Native Americans used to ensure a continuous food supply was to plant their crops in more than one place, hoping that if one crop failed, another would survive. However, since the soil was rich and not easily exhausted, the same patch of ground could be cultivated year after year, whereas in the woodlands of the eastern United States it was necessary to abandon a plot of ground after a few years of farming. In the Southwest, often two successive crops were planted each year.

questions.stem: What does the passage mainly discuss?

options.B: Irrigation techniques used by the Hopi
options.C: Soil quality in the American Southwest
options.D: Native American methods of storing emergency food supplies

questions.analysis: 题型：主旨题 答案: (A) Agricultural methods of Native Americans 原文定位: 首段：提出干旱环境下的农业挑战（水问题）； 第二段：详述水利技术（洪泛种植、堤坝、霍皮人案例）； 第三段：补充风险分散种植与土壤管理策略。 选项分析: 全文三段围绕原住民农业策略展开：水资源管理（核心）、多地点种植、土壤可持续利用。选项(B)(C)(D)仅为局部细节。

questions.stem: The word "solve" is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: 题型：词汇题 答案: (D) deal with 原文定位: 第二段首句 "Several techniques were developed to solve the water problem." 选项分析: 语境中“solve”指应对水问题（如洪水/干旱），而非彻底解决。(D) "deal with"（处理）最贴合；选项(A)(B)偏离文意。

questions.stem: Planting in the floodplains was not ideal because

options.A: the amount of water could not be controlled
options.B: the crops could be eaten by wild animals
options.C: the floodplains were too remote to be cultivated frequently
options.D: corn grows better at high elevations

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文定位: 第二段对比句 "The simplest was to plant... wait for annual floods. A less dangerous technique was to build dikes... control the flooding." 原文通过“less dangerous”暗示洪泛种植的风险性（依赖自然洪水，水量不可控），选项(A)直接对应；其他选项无依据。

questions.stem: Why did farmers in the eastern woodlands periodically abandon their fields?

options.C: They wanted a longer growing season.
options.D: The minerals in the soil were exhausted.

questions.analysis: 题型：细节题 原文定位: 第三段对比句 "in the Southwest... soil not easily exhausted... whereas in the eastern woodlands necessary to abandon a plot... after a few years." 东西部土壤对比明确：东部因土壤肥力耗尽需轮耕，西南部因土壤富矿可连作。选项(D)为原文同义替换。

questions.stem: Why does the author mention the Hopi people's use of a "checkerboard pattern" with small dikes in paragraph 2?

options.A: To compare the Hopi technique unfavorably to other groups' dam systems
options.B: To illustrate how Native Americans adapted water control methods to local conditions
options.C: To demonstrate a method for protecting individual plants from flooding
options.D: To argue that complex engineering was necessary for agriculture

questions.analysis: 题型：修辞目的题 原文定位: 第二段细节句 "The Hopi... each enclosing only one or two stalks of maize... These dikes protected plants against excessive flooding." 作者用霍皮案例具象化前文论点（堤坝防洪），通过“包围单株玉米”的细节，说明技术如何微观保护作物。 选项分析: A 无比较倾向（后文用"while"中立并列其他技术）； B 未提地域适应性（本段焦点是技术原理）； D 偏离主旨（前文强调技术可简可繁）。
